verification: Project-authored guidance reviewed against the recorded source snapshot. Examples are syntax-checked, not tested in-game; specific engine caveats are identified where relevant.

guides.name: CreateUnit
guides.summary: Create a unit of a chosen type for a player at map coordinates.

parameters.id: The owning player handle, such as Player(0), rather than a numeric player slot.
parameters.unitid: The integer raw code of a unit type available in the map.

guides.returns: The newly created unit handle. Retain it if your system will later issue orders, change fields or remove the unit.
usage: Choose an existing unit type and owner, then create the unit from synchronized map code.
Keep permanent gameplay units for their intended lifetime. For temporary units, keep a reference so the creating system can remove them.
guides.ownership: This creates a unit. The system that creates a temporary unit should arrange RemoveUnit when finished. Clearing a variable does not remove the unit from the map.
pitfalls: Do not pass a display name such as Footman as the unit type. Use its raw code.
Do not remove a permanent gameplay unit merely to tidy a local variable.
jassNotes: Write a four-character raw code as an integer literal, for example 'hfoo'. Clear local handle references when finished with them.
luaNotes: Convert the raw code with FourCC("hfoo"). An ordinary string is not the required integer unit type.
unverified: Invalid type IDs and exact placement around blocked terrain have not been tested in-game for this snapshot.

guides.name: RemoveUnit
guides.summary: Remove an existing unit when its owning system no longer needs it.

parameters.whichUnit: The unit to remove; ensure it belongs to the system performing cleanup.

guides.returns: No value. The passed unit must no longer be used by your system.
usage: Use this to retire temporary units or deliberately remove a map unit.
Clear stored references after removal so later callbacks do not try to use the old unit.
guides.ownership: Removes the unit itself. It does not release unrelated groups, locations or timers that your code created while working with that unit.
pitfalls: GroupRemoveUnit removes group membership; it does not remove a unit from the map.
If the design requires a unit to die, consider KillUnit. Do not use removal as a substitute for a death workflow.
jassNotes: Set stored unit variables to null after removal when your system no longer needs them.
luaNotes: Assign nil to stored references after removal. Destroying the engine unit does not automatically erase references from Lua tables.
unverified: Death-event ordering and removal during other running callbacks are not established by this guide.

guides.name: GetUnitX
guides.summary: Read a unit's current horizontal map coordinate without allocating a location.

parameters.whichUnit: The existing unit whose position you want to read.

guides.returns: A real number: the unit's horizontal coordinate at the time of the call.
usage: Read both coordinates when a calculation needs a position pair.
Read again when you need an updated position; stored numbers do not follow a moving unit.
guides.ownership: Returns a number and borrows the unit. There is no temporary location to remove and no unit ownership transfer.
pitfalls: A coordinate is not a location handle. Do not pass it to RemoveLocation.
This coordinate does not include terrain height or flying height.

guides.name: GetUnitY
guides.summary: Read a unit's current vertical map coordinate without allocating a location.

parameters.whichUnit: The existing unit whose position you want to read.

guides.returns: A real number: the unit's vertical coordinate at the time of the call.
usage: Read both coordinates when a calculation needs a position pair.
Read again when you need an updated position; stored numbers do not follow a moving unit.
guides.ownership: Returns a number and borrows the unit. There is no temporary location to remove and no unit ownership transfer.
pitfalls: A coordinate is not a location handle. Do not pass it to RemoveLocation.
This coordinate does not include terrain height or flying height.

guides.name: SetUnitPosition
guides.summary: Reposition an existing unit to a requested map location.
guides.returns: No value. Read GetUnitX and GetUnitY afterwards if the resulting position matters.
usage: Use this for deliberate repositioning. Use a movement order when the unit should walk to its destination.
Treat the requested coordinates as a placement request; terrain and placement constraints can affect the result.
guides.ownership: Modifies a borrowed unit. It creates no location or other temporary handle that needs cleanup.
pitfalls: Do not expect a walking animation or a path to be followed as with a move order.
Do not assume the final coordinates exactly match the requested coordinates.
unverified: Precise placement near obstacles, cliffs and map edges has not been tested in-game for this snapshot.

guides.name: CreateTimer
guides.summary: Allocate a timer that can later run a callback after a delay.
guides.returns: A new timer handle. Creating it alone does not start a countdown.
usage: Create a timer, then call TimerStart with a delay and callback.
Decide whether the timer belongs to a single operation or is a persistent timer shared by a system.
guides.ownership: The creating system owns the timer. DestroyTimer releases it when no longer needed, including after a one-shot countdown.
pitfalls: An unstarted timer does not invoke any callback.
Repeatedly replacing a stored timer without destroying the old one leaves the earlier timers owned but unreachable.

guides.name: TimerStart
guides.summary: Start or restart a timer and choose the function to run when it expires.

parameters.whichTimer: An existing timer, usually allocated with CreateTimer.
parameters.timeout: Delay in seconds; use a positive interval for ordinary countdowns.
parameters.periodic: True to repeat the countdown; false to run it once.
parameters.handlerFunc: Callback function value, passed without calling it.

guides.returns: No value. The callback runs later when the timer expires.
usage: Create the timer first and pass a no-argument callback. Starting the same timer again configures that timer rather than allocating another one.
For a one-shot operation, destroy the timer in its callback. For a periodic operation, define a stop and cleanup path.
Capture event data before leaving an event action; the later timer callback is a different context.
guides.ownership: Does not allocate a second timer. A one-shot timer still needs DestroyTimer after it finishes; periodic timers need an explicit owner that stops and destroys them.
pitfalls: Calling the callback while supplying this argument executes it now instead of registering it.
Do not assume a paused timer and a newly restarted timer preserve the same countdown state.
jassNotes: Pass function CallbackName and declare the callback before the initializer that refers to it.
luaNotes: Pass a function value or closure, for example function() ... end, rather than CallbackName().
unverified: Zero or negative delays, scheduling precision and reentrant restart behavior have not been tested here.

guides.name: PauseTimer
guides.summary: Pause a timer without releasing its handle.

parameters.whichTimer: The existing timer whose countdown should be paused.

guides.returns: No value. The timer remains allocated.
usage: Pause a retained timer when its system needs to suspend it. ResumeTimer is the related operation for continuing it.
The cleanup example pauses the timer before destroying it; pausing alone is not cleanup.
guides.ownership: Borrows an existing timer. Its owner must still call DestroyTimer when the timer is no longer needed.
pitfalls: Do not lose the timer reference after pausing it; it still occupies an engine handle.
Do not destroy a shared timer just because the current caller pauses it.

guides.name: DestroyTimer
guides.summary: Release a timer after its owning operation has finished.

parameters.whichTimer: The timer owned by the system performing cleanup.

guides.returns: No value. Stop using the timer handle after this call.
usage: Retain the handle until the operation completes, then pause and destroy it as shown in the example.
For a one-shot callback, GetExpiredTimer can identify the timer to release.
guides.ownership: Releases the engine timer. Clear stored references afterwards. Callback-created units, groups and other resources need their own cleanup.
pitfalls: A one-shot timer does not release itself merely because its callback ran.
Do not destroy a timer borrowed from another system without agreeing on ownership.
unverified: This guide does not establish cancellation behavior for callback code that is already running.

guides.name: GetExpiredTimer
guides.summary: Read the timer associated with the timer-expiration callback currently running.
guides.returns: The existing timer for the current expiration callback, rather than a newly allocated timer.
usage: Call inside a TimerStart callback when you need to identify or destroy that callback's timer.
Keep application state separately when several timers share the same callback.
guides.ownership: Borrows the callback's timer. Destroy it only when this callback owns completion of that timer; periodic timers may need to keep running.
pitfalls: This is not a way to find the most recently created timer.
Do not defer this getter to unrelated code and expect the original timer context to remain available.
unverified: Values returned outside a matching expiration callback are not established here; do not rely on a null fallback.

guides.name: CreateGroup
guides.summary: Allocate an empty collection of unit references.
guides.returns: A new empty group handle ready for adding or enumerating units.
usage: Create a scratch group, populate it, process its members, then destroy it.
Retain and clear a group when a system deliberately reuses the collection.
guides.ownership: The creator owns the collection. DestroyGroup releases it; the units inside remain separate gameplay objects.
pitfalls: A new group has no members until you add or enumerate them.
Dropping a variable does not release the engine group.

guides.name: GroupEnumUnitsInRange
guides.summary: Fill a supplied group with units found around a map coordinate.

parameters.whichGroup: An existing group that receives the enumeration results. Use a dedicated scratch group.
parameters.x: Horizontal coordinate of the search center.
parameters.y: Vertical coordinate of the search center.
parameters.radius: Search radius in map units; supply a nonnegative distance.
parameters.filter: Optional boolean-expression filter. With no filter, apply your own gameplay checks to the results.

guides.returns: No value. Process the units through the supplied group.
usage: Allocate a group before enumerating. Use GroupClear before reusing a collection whose previous contents are no longer needed.
Apply ownership, alive-state and unit-type checks required by your game rules. Do not assume a range search already enforces them.
Use GetFilterUnit in a filter callback, GetEnumUnit in ForGroup, or FirstOfGroup for a loop that removes processed members.
guides.ownership: Borrows the receiving group and its units. The caller still owns the group and any separately created filter expression. The example passes no filter and destroys its scratch group.
pitfalls: Do not pass an uninitialized group as the output collection.
Do not assume repeated enumeration accumulates a union. If you need a union, build that membership explicitly.
jassNotes: Pass null when no filter is needed. A code callback is not itself a boolexpr; use the appropriate expression constructor if filtering.
luaNotes: Pass nil for no filter. A Lua function is not itself the boolexpr handle required by this parameter.
unverified: Exact boundary inclusion, collision-size effects and special unit visibility cases have not been tested for this snapshot.

guides.name: ForGroup
guides.summary: Run a callback for the units in a group.

parameters.whichGroup: An existing populated group to enumerate.
parameters.callback: No-argument callback that reads its current member with GetEnumUnit.

guides.returns: No value. Work is performed by the callback.
usage: Populate the group first. Inside the callback, use GetEnumUnit to read the current unit.
Keep the callback immediate and avoid waits or mutation of the enumerated collection. Use a FirstOfGroup loop when membership must change as you process it.
guides.ownership: Borrows the group and its unit members. The caller retains responsibility for DestroyGroup; enumeration does not remove units from the map.
pitfalls: Do not use GetTriggerUnit to identify a group member. It describes a different context.
Passing an empty group does not select units automatically.
jassNotes: Pass function CallbackName, with its declaration before the caller.
luaNotes: Pass a function value; invoke GetEnumUnit inside that function.

guides.name: GetEnumUnit
guides.summary: Read the unit currently being processed by a ForGroup callback.
guides.returns: The existing unit for the active group-enumeration callback.
usage: Call inside the callback passed to ForGroup.
Pass the returned unit explicitly to code that needs it after the callback; do not expect enumeration context to persist.
guides.ownership: Borrows a group member. Reading it allocates nothing and does not transfer ownership of the unit.
pitfalls: Do not call RemoveUnit solely to clean up a borrowed enumeration result.
GetFilterUnit is for filtering and GetTriggerUnit is for unit events; neither replaces this getter in ForGroup.
unverified: The return value outside an enumeration callback is not established here.

guides.name: FirstOfGroup
guides.summary: Read one member of a group without removing it.
guides.returns: A unit member, or no unit when the group is empty. Do not build logic around a particular member order.
usage: For a draining loop, fetch one unit, exit if empty, remove that member, then process it.
The linked range-search example removes each fetched member before the next iteration.
guides.ownership: Borrows a unit reference. GroupRemoveUnit changes membership; DestroyGroup releases the collection. Neither operation removes the unit from the map.
pitfalls: Calling FirstOfGroup repeatedly without removing or otherwise changing the member can create an endless loop.
Do not confuse removing a member with calling RemoveUnit.
jassNotes: Check the returned unit against null to finish a draining loop.
luaNotes: Check the returned unit against nil to finish a draining loop.
unverified: Groups containing units already removed from the map need separate validation; stale-member behavior is not covered here.

guides.name: GroupClear
guides.summary: Empty a group while keeping the collection available for reuse.

parameters.whichGroup: The group whose memberships should be discarded.

guides.returns: No value. The group remains allocated and can receive units again.
usage: Use when a retained scratch group should start with no previous members.
Destroy the group when your system no longer needs the collection itself.
guides.ownership: Clears references from the group without removing its units from the map. The group owner still owes DestroyGroup at the end of its lifetime.
pitfalls: GroupClear does not free the group handle.
Clearing a group is not a way to delete all its units.

guides.name: DestroyGroup
guides.summary: Release a group collection after processing its unit references.

parameters.whichGroup: The group owned by the system performing cleanup.

guides.returns: No value. The group handle must no longer be used.
usage: Process the results, then release a temporary scratch group.
Use GroupClear instead when a retained group must be emptied and reused.
guides.ownership: Destroys the collection, not its units. Clear stored references to the destroyed group; do not destroy collections borrowed from another system.
pitfalls: DestroyGroup does not remove or kill its members.
Do not call GroupClear or enumerate into a group after destroying it.

guides.name: CreateTrigger
guides.summary: Allocate a trigger that can own event registrations and actions.
guides.returns: A new trigger handle. Add the events and actions needed for it to respond.
usage: Create the trigger, register an event, then add its callback action during setup.
Register a persistent listener once during map initialization; retain temporary listeners when you will need to destroy them.
guides.ownership: The creating system owns the trigger. A deliberate map-lifetime listener stays alive; a temporary listener should be destroyed when finished.
pitfalls: Creating a trigger alone does not register it for any event.
Running the initializer repeatedly creates additional listeners and duplicate responses.

guides.name: TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent
guides.summary: Register a trigger for a unit event belonging to one player slot.

parameters.whichTrigger: An existing trigger that should receive the event.
parameters.whichPlayer: The player handle whose units are being observed.
parameters.whichPlayerUnitEvent: A player-unit event constant, such as EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_DEATH.
parameters.filter: Optional boolexpr limiting eligible units. The example uses no filter.

guides.returns: An event handle representing the registration, rather than a unit or the trigger itself.
usage: Register the event and attach an action. Read the unit in that action using the event getter appropriate to that event.
One call targets one player. The example loops across player slots; TriggerRegisterAnyUnitEventBJ is a helper for that setup.
guides.ownership: Attaches a registration to the supplied trigger. Manage the trigger lifetime with DestroyTrigger. Any separately created filter expression needs its own ownership plan; the example avoids one.
pitfalls: A numeric player index is not a player handle; use Player(index).
Registering the same listener repeatedly can produce duplicate responses.
jassNotes: Use null for an omitted filter.
luaNotes: Use nil for an omitted filter.

guides.name: TriggerAddAction
guides.summary: Attach a callback to an existing trigger.

parameters.whichTrigger: The trigger whose responses should include this action.
parameters.actionFunc: Callback function value to run when the trigger executes its actions.

guides.returns: A triggeraction handle identifying the attached action. Keep it if you need TriggerRemoveAction later.
usage: Register an event and add an action during listener setup. Adding the action does not execute it immediately.
Read event responses while handling that event; pass captured values into deferred timer work.
guides.ownership: The action belongs to the trigger. Remove a specific action with TriggerRemoveAction when needed, or destroy a finished temporary trigger. Resources allocated by actions need separate cleanup.
pitfalls: Passing the result of calling a function does not register that function as the action.
Do not attach another copy of an action every time the event occurs.
jassNotes: Pass function ActionName and declare ActionName before the setup function.
luaNotes: Pass ActionName or a closure, rather than ActionName().

guides.name: GetTriggerUnit
guides.summary: Read the unit associated with the unit event currently being handled.
guides.returns: The existing unit supplied by the current unit-event context. This is not a newly created unit.
usage: Use in an action registered for a unit event. The example reads the dying unit from a player-unit death event.
Store the unit in a local and pass it explicitly to later work instead of calling this getter from an unrelated timer callback.
guides.ownership: Borrows the event unit. Do not remove it merely because the action is finished reading it.
pitfalls: This is not the currently selected unit or the current group-enumeration member.
Do not assume every trigger event provides a unit response.
unverified: No safe fallback value is promised outside a matching unit-event context. Use this getter only where the registered event supplies it.

guides.name: DestroyTrigger
guides.summary: Release a trigger after its listener is no longer needed.

parameters.whichTrigger: The trigger owned by the system performing cleanup.

guides.returns: No value. Stop using the trigger after destruction.
usage: Keep a reference to a temporary listener until it can be retired.
Keep deliberately persistent listeners alive for the map lifetime instead of destroying them at the end of their initializer.
guides.ownership: Releases the trigger and its attached listener setup. Timers, groups, locations or units created separately by its actions remain the responsibility of their owning systems.
pitfalls: Clearing a variable alone does not retire an active listener.
Do not destroy a shared trigger simply because one caller is finished with it.
unverified: Do not rely on this call to cancel action code that is already running; that behavior has not been tested here.

guides.name: TriggerRegisterAnyUnitEventBJ
guides.summary: Register one player-unit event across the player slots using a Blizzard helper.

parameters.trig: The existing trigger to register across player slots.
parameters.whichEvent: A player-unit event constant, such as EVENT_PLAYER_UNIT_DEATH.

guides.returns: No value. Unlike the single-player native, this helper does not return an event handle.
usage: Use for a listener that needs the same unit event across players, then attach an action once.
The local helper uses bj_MAX_PLAYER_SLOTS to iterate the slots and delegates registration to TriggerRegisterPlayerUnitEvent without a filter. This is setup convenience, not a different kind of event.
guides.ownership: Adds registrations to the supplied trigger. It does not create a new trigger or unit; the caller still controls the trigger lifetime.
pitfalls: Do not call this helper separately for each player; it already iterates the slots.
Do not add the same action once per slot when one trigger action is enough.

guides.name: Location
guides.summary: Allocate a point handle from two map coordinates.
guides.returns: A new location handle containing the position.
usage: Use when an API specifically requires a location handle. If an API accepts numeric coordinates, pass the numbers directly.
Keep the point until its last use, then remove it.
guides.ownership: Allocates an owned location. Pair it with RemoveLocation; clearing a variable does not release the engine point.
pitfalls: Repeatedly constructing points without removing them leaves allocated handles behind.
A location is not a unit and does not move a unit merely by being created.

guides.name: GetUnitLoc
guides.summary: Allocate a location containing a snapshot of a unit's position.

parameters.whichUnit: The existing unit whose current position should be copied.

guides.returns: A newly allocated location, separate from the unit. It does not automatically follow subsequent movement.
usage: Use when another function needs a location handle for the unit's current position.
If you need only coordinates, use GetUnitX and GetUnitY to avoid allocating a point.
guides.ownership: The caller owns the returned location and must RemoveLocation after the last use. The source unit is borrowed and must not be removed as location cleanup.
pitfalls: Each call creates a new location, even for the same unit. Reusing the variable does not release the old point.
Do not keep using a removed location.

guides.name: RemoveLocation
guides.summary: Release a temporary location after its last use.

parameters.whichLocation: The location owned by the system performing cleanup.

guides.returns: No value. The point handle must no longer be used.
usage: Read any needed coordinates before releasing the point.
Remove points created by Location or GetUnitLoc when no later operation needs them.
guides.ownership: Releases the point handle, not a unit or terrain feature at that coordinate. Shared points require an agreed owner; do not remove a borrowed point arbitrarily.
pitfalls: Setting a variable to null or nil is not a substitute for RemoveLocation.
Do not call a location getter with the old handle after removing it.
jassNotes: After RemoveLocation, clear local or stored references with set point = null when finished.
luaNotes: After RemoveLocation, clear retained references with point = nil. Lua garbage collection does not replace engine-handle cleanup.
